chunks: From him, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The people of Mecca complete the prayer at Arafat.' He said, 'Woe to them or woe to them! And which journey is more severe than it? They do not complete [the prayer].'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj
key_terms.وَيْلَهُمْ: Woe to them (an expression of rebuke or warning)
key_terms.يُتِمُّونَ: They complete (prayer, i.e., pray four rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayer at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that travelers at Arafat must perform the full four-rak'ah prayer, rejecting the practice of shortening it (qasr) because the journey to Arafat is considered exceptionally arduous, thus qualifying as a severe travel state. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction that the intensity of the journey, rather than just distance, determines the status of travel, ensuring the prayer remains complete despite the pilgrim's fatigue.
